artifacts.summary: Confirms the helper/contract/14-call-site state is already correct, identifies lint-state-writer-boundary.sh/lint-hook-registration-paths.sh as the structural template to clone, and surfaces two concrete scoping risks: a naive broad scan corpus would false-positive on dozens of unrelated test-assertion lines plus an out-of-scope pre-existing site, and verify-deploy.sh's --only-gate range is already hardcoded stale (rejects gate 24 live) and must be widened for gate 25 to be selectable.

memory_candidates.content: This codebase's 'boundary lint' family (lint-state-writer-boundary.sh, lint-hook-registration-paths.sh, lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh, lint-directory-pathspec-boundary.sh) shares one structural template: a resolve_project_root helper robust to running from either the deployed or source-store location, a DEFAULT_SCAN + positional-SCAN_PATHS-override pair, a two-layer detection model (Layer 1: broad CANDIDATE_PATTERN regex -> classify_line narrowing to VIOLATION or EXEMPT:<reason>; Layer 2: a file-level EXCLUDED_FILES allowlist where every entry states WHY it is exempt in a comment, never a bare path), and echo -e "${RED}[VIOLATION]${NC} $file:$lineno: ..." emission. Their own test suites build every fixture (both polarities) inside a mktemp -d WORKDIR at test-run time and pass it as a positional path override -- no fixture file is ever committed to the repo. Reuse this template wholesale for any new source-text-shape lint rather than inventing a new structure.

When designing a new corpus-scanning lint for a narrowly-contractual shell-script shape (a producer/consumer contract documented for one specific subsystem, not a codebase-wide rule), prefer a hand-picked explicit file list as the default scan corpus over a directory walk (@extensions/@repo/a whole scripts/ subtree). A broad walk force-forward false-positives on syntactically-similar but semantically-unrelated code -- in this codebase specifically, ordinary test-assertion lines across scripts/tests/*.sh routinely grep a test subject's own [FAIL]/[VIOLATION]-shaped output for assertion purposes, which looks identical to the dangerous shape a verdict-extraction lint is designed to catch but is a completely different, legitimate idiom. A narrow corpus matching the contract document's own stated scope avoids inventing an open-ended allowlist reactively.
